screening_results.reason: Task-based fMRI study of arithmetic word problem solving reporting neural activation. Abstract explicitly confirms task-based fMRI (I1), problem-solving task (I2), and task-related brain activation results (I4). The abstract does not explicitly state the sample are healthy adults, so I3 is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI and PET study using the Tower of London problem-solving task and reports task-related brain activation. It does not explicitly state participant health status (healthy adults not confirmed), so full-text review is needed to confirm I3.

Abstract reports a human virtual-maze navigation study addressing parahippocampal involvement, but does not explicitly state imaging modality (fMRI/PET), whether the task qualifies as problem-solving/reasoning, or that participants were healthy adults. Information is insufficient to confirm inclusion criteria; include for full-text review to determine I1–I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human problem-solving that reports task-related brain activation (I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults (I3 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study of problem solving (Japanese riddles) in human participants and reports task-related brain activations (right hippocampus and cortex). The abstract does not explicitly state the health status or age of participants, so inclusion of healthy adults is not confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review to verify I3.

Meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult controls), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Unclear whether the virtual maze task qualifies as a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2) because it focuses on egocentric spatial navigation/learning; include for full-text review to determine I2.

Task-based fMRI study with 28 adult participants performing an arithmetic problem-solving task; reports brain activation results linking left angular gyrus to fact retrieval. All inclusion criteria are met (I1-I4). No exclusion criteria apply.

E2 applies: sample are high school students (no evidence of healthy adults). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI with BOLD), I2 (geometric analogical reasoning task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I3 (no healthy adult group reported).

Task-based neuroimaging study (fMRI/PET implied) with healthy adult participants performing algebraic problem-solving and reporting task-related brain activations; meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria evident.

Abstract reports an event-related task-based fMRI study of verbal insight/problem-solving (solving Chinese riddles) and reports task-related activations. Participant health/age is not specified, so I3 (healthy adults) is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract reports task-based BOLD fMRI contrasts during a problem-solving (Chinese logogriphs/riddles) task and presents task-related brain activations. It does not explicitly state the participant health status (healthy adults not confirmed), so inclusion criterion I3 is uncertain; include for full-text review to verify participant sample.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) in which human participants performed a scientific inventive problem-solving task (I2). Thirty-two participants are reported (healthy adult sample implied) (I3). The abstract reports task-related BOLD activation results and specific brain regions (I4). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of the Tower of London problem-solving task, reports task-related brain activation results, and involves healthy adult participants (individual differences in working memory measured). No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study does not investigate problem-solving/reasoning tasks (EIDs: none). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based PET). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (not a problem-solving task; focuses on appetitive/food stimuli), I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated in abstract), I4 (task-related activation not clearly reported in abstract). No exclusion criteria clearly met based on abstract.

Task-based fMRI (reversal learning) and PET were used in healthy adults and the abstract reports task-related BOLD/PET results. It is unclear whether the imaging task qualifies as a problem-solving/reasoning task (they measured fluid intelligence separately), so include for full-text review to resolve I2.

Excluded: does not investigate problem-solving tasks. Inclusion met: I1 (PET study). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated), I4 (task-related activation not clearly reported). No exclusion criteria clearly met (E1,E2 not shown).

This is a task-based fMRI study that reports task-related brain activation and includes a healthy adult control group. The abstract does not clearly indicate whether the egocentric virtual maze task constitutes a problem-solving/reasoning task as defined by the review, so full-text review is needed to assess I2.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (PET study), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (participants performing a problem-solving or reasoning task) — study used histamine-induced itch, not problem solving.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI of the Tower of London (a problem-solving task) and measures brain activation, but it does not clearly state whether healthy adult participants are included. Include for full-text review to confirm presence of a healthy adult sample.

Task-based fMRI study of visuospatial analogical reasoning in humans that reports task-related brain activation (RLPFC, IFG, inferior parietal cortex). Participants are healthy adults (typical fMRI cognitive study). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based PET study examining cerebral activation during arithmetic tasks (recitation and calculation), indicating task-related brain activation. The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults, so full-text is needed to confirm I3.

Excluded: E2 met — study involves chronic tinnitus patients and therapeutic rTMS, with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (problem-solving task), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (task-related activation).

PET study mapping brain activation during the PASAT (meets I1 and I4). The PASAT involves arithmetic but abstract does not explicitly confirm it as a problem-solving/reasoning task per inclusion I2 nor explicitly state participants were healthy adults (I3). No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to clarify I2 and I3.

EXCLUDE because the study uses resting/structural MRI and FDG-PET in bvFTD patients and controls, not a task-based fMRI/PET paradigm and it does not involve a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion met: I3 (includes healthy adult controls). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (not task-based PET/fMRI), I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (no task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based PET study), I3 (includes healthy adult controls). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task performed), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants performing an integration verification (problem-solving) task; reports task-related brain activation patterns consistent with problem-solving. Fits all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning in human adults reporting task-related brain activation across problem-solving phases; meets all inclusion criteria (I1-I4) and no exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the task involved audiovisual sexual stimuli inducing penile erection, not a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based PET study) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no problem-solving task) and I3 (healthy adult sample not clearly demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1), participants performed a reasoning/problem-solving task (RSPM) (I2), includes a healthy adult control group (non-autistic participants) (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports human mental-arithmetic task and presents task-related brain activation results, satisfying I2 and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state use of fMRI/PET (I1) or specify healthy adult sample (I3), so full-text review is needed to confirm those criteria.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study using simplified Sudoku puzzles with participants performing problem-solving and reports task-related ROI activations, satisfying I1, I2, and I4. Participant health status (I3: healthy adults) is not explicitly stated, so include for full-text review to confirm sample characteristics.

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing a fluid analogy task (problem solving/reasoning) with healthy adult participants; reports task-related BOLD activation results. Abstract satisfies all inclusion criteria for full-text review.

Exclusion E2 met: study includes only children (ages 7-9), no healthy adult sample. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing problem-solving/arithmetic), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (does not include healthy adults).

Task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Tower of London) reporting task-related dlPFC activation in human participants. The abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of a healthy adult sample, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Abstract reports an fMRI task-based study where human participants performed an anagram (problem-solving) task and authors report task-related brain activation (insula, PFC, ACC). No exclusion criteria apply. All inclusion criteria (I1-I4) are satisfied based on abstract information.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based PET study that reports task-specific brain activations (I1, I4). However, it does not specify that the tasks involved problem-solving/reasoning (I2 not demonstrated) nor explicitly state participants were healthy adults (I3 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to confirm I2 and I3; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of problem-solving in healthy elderly adults and reports BOLD responses in PCC/precuneus, satisfying all inclusion criteria (I1-I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study (n=75) with human participants performing a novel mathematical/problem-solving task, includes an adult group, and reports task-related brain activation (RLPFC and other regions). Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI case study in a healthy adult performing planning/problem-solving tasks (Tower of London and VR navigation) that reports task-related brain activation. Meets I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met; include for full-text review to extract detailed data and confirm suitability for meta-analysis.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (includes healthy age- and gender-matched control group). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a task-based PET study — molecular imaging tracer study), I2 (participants did not perform a problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation).

E2: The study samples are children (developmental dyscalculia and typically developing children) and do not include any healthy adult group. Included criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing problem-solving tasks), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI task where human participants solved Chinese riddles (problem-solving), with stimulus- and response-locked analyses and reported task-related brain activations. However, the abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults, so full-text review is required to confirm I3.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving in human participants (strong and weak problem-solvers), includes healthy adult participants, and reports task-related brain activation results (regional activations during planning and performance phases). No exclusion criteria are met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (study includes healthy adult controls/GBA-mutation carriers). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based study; PET was at rest), I2 (participants did not perform a problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (no task-related activation reported; measures are resting rCBF and dopamine synthesis).

Study is a PET drug-challenge measuring THC-induced dopamine release, not a task-based problem-solving or reasoning paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (PET study), I3 (includes healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants performing an analogical reasoning task with reported task-related activations, meeting I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not specify whether participants were healthy adults (I3 unclear), so include for full-text review to confirm health status.

Study used vibrotactile sensory stimulation, not a problem-solving or reasoning task, so it does not meet I2. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based PET), I3 (healthy adult volunteers), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (none applied).

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in 15 normal (healthy) adult subjects performing problem-solving (anagram) tasks and reports task-related brain activation results (right ventral lateral PFC); all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the task is single-word reading (language), not a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (PET study), I3 (includes healthy nonstuttering adult group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1/E2 apply).

Task-based fMRI study with healthy young and older adult participants performing a virtual navigation learning task; reports task-related hippocampus and caudate nucleus activation. Satisfies I1, I3, and I4. It is unclear from the abstract whether the navigation task fits the review's definition of 'problem-solving or reasoning' (I2), so include for full-text review to resolve this uncertainty.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of spatial problem solving and reports atypical task-related brain activation (meets I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not clearly state whether a healthy adult control group was included (I3 not demonstrated). Include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult sample.

The study used a covert word-generation (language) task, not a problem-solving/reasoning task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based PET) and I4 (reports task-related activation). I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task) is not met. I3 (explicit healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

No problem-solving or reasoning task reported (I2 not met) and does not report task-related brain activation for a problem-solving task (I4 not demonstrated). Inclusion met: I1 (PET study) and I3 (healthy adult participants). No exclusion criteria met (E1, E2).

Excluded because inclusion criteria not met: study includes a healthy adult control group (I3 met) but is not a task-based PET/fMRI study (I1 not met), participants are children with epilepsy and did not perform a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2 not met), and it reports sedation-related hypometabolism not task-related activation (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study does not involve a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants reporting task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria are met (none of E1/E2 apply). The task is navigation/route learning and resting-state connectivity, not problem-solving as required by the review.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adults, reports task-related brain activation. Abstract indicates navigation and shortcut-finding (may be a form of problem-solving), but it is not explicit whether the task meets the review's definition of problem-solving; include for full-text review to determine I2.

All inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI study (I1) of humans performing a problem-solving/reasoning task (modified Raven's Matrices) (I2), includes matched healthy adult controls (I3), and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes PET neuroimaging synchronized with cognitive measures in OCD but does not clearly state a task-based PET design, a problem-solving/reasoning task, or inclusion of healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria are clearly met; insufficient information to determine inclusion from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

PET study reporting task-related brain activations during deductive and probabilistic reasoning tasks in human participants. Abstract does not explicitly state sample health status, so inclusion criterion I3 (healthy adults) is uncertain; full-text review needed to confirm. Included for full-text screening.

Abstract reports an event-related task-based fMRI study in which healthy adult participants (n=16) performed inductive and deductive reasoning (problem-solving) and reports task-related brain activation results—meets all inclusion criteria.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of participants passively viewing arithmetic expressions and reports task-related brain activation (adaptation in fronto-parietal number-related regions). However the abstract does not specify participant health status/age (healthy adults not explicitly stated), so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Study uses task-based fMRI with healthy adults and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4), but the task is navigation/landmark learning and recognition rather than a problem-solving or reasoning task; inclusion criterion I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based PET study—uses PET for receptor occupancy/pharmacology), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task described), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). I3 (healthy adults) not clearly demonstrated in abstract.
Task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning (problem solving) in humans; includes healthy adult participants and reports task-related brain activation (parametric ROI results).

Task-based fMRI study (participants performed Wason Selection reasoning task during fMRI) reporting task-related brain activations. Abstract does not specify participant health status, so inclusion criterion I3 (healthy adults) is unclear. Include for full-text review to confirm health status.

EXCLUDED: This is a resting-state FDG-PET study in relapsing-remitting MS patients with healthy controls; it is not a task-based fMRI/PET study nor does it involve participants performing a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based imaging), I2 (problem-solving task), I4 (task-related activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Relevant task-based fMRI study in healthy adults; includes explicit problem-solving task (blocked-route problem-solving) along with other spatial tasks and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

I1, I3, and I4 are satisfied (task-based fMRI, healthy adult participants, reports task-related activations). I2 is not met: the task involves pain/hyperalgesia stimulation, not problem-solving or reasoning. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants performing analogizing (a reasoning/problem-solving) tasks and describes task-related neural activations. It does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults, so include for full-text review to confirm I3 (healthy adults).

Abstract reports PET during general anaesthesia with xenon to study regional CBF and coupling; no task-based paradigm or problem-solving task is described, and no task-related activation results are reported. Likely participants were anaesthetized rather than performing tasks. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria for task-based problem-solving studies.

Excluded because the study examines spatial navigation, not a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). Abstract indicates task-related brain activation was examined (I4 met). Other inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (imaging modality fMRI/PET not specified) and I3 (presence of healthy adult sample not confirmed). No exclusion criteria clearly met (exclusion_criteria_applied: []).

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants reporting task-related neural activation. Abstract lacks clear evidence that the scanned task is a problem-solving/reasoning task (n-back working-memory may not meet 'problem solving' definition), so include for full-text review to verify I2.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study of human subjects performing propositional analogy and semantic reasoning tasks, with reported task-related brain activation results. It does not explicitly state participant health status, so full text review is needed to confirm healthy adult sample.

Event-related fMRI study of a nonverbal analogical reasoning (problem-solving) task; reports task-related increases in prefrontal activation. Abstract does not explicitly state participant health status (healthy adults), so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning with 12 healthy adult participants that reports BOLD activation results across brain regions, meeting all inclusion criteria (I1–I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

This PET study measured baseline D2/3 receptor binding in healthy adults and did not use a task-based paradigm or report task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (problem-solving task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Not a task-based imaging study of problem solving. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based PET/fMRI study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task performed), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with participants performing date/mental-arithmetic problems and task-related parietal activation (I1, I2, I4). However it is unclear whether a healthy adult sample or control group was included (I3 not demonstrated). Inclusion uncertain from abstract so include for full-text review.
Study is not task-based and does not involve participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met: I1, I2, I4.

Excluded because the study used EEG/ERP (event-related potentials), not task-based fMRI or PET, so inclusion criterion I1 is not met. The abstract reports human reasoning tasks and task-related brain activation (I2 and I4 met). Participant sample not specified as healthy adults, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which healthy adult participants performed algebra problem-solving; it describes differential brain activation and cognitive modeling relating to task manipulations, satisfying I1–I4.

EXCLUDED because E2: study includes only children (2nd–3rd graders, ages 7–9) and contains no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed an arithmetic problem-solving task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (at least one group of healthy adults).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning (a problem-solving/reasoning task) in human participants, describes brain activation results, and implies healthy adult subjects; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (BOLD), participants performed the Tower of London problem-solving task, includes a healthy adult control group (10 healthy male volunteers), and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract/title indicates a PET behavioral challenge (I1), but provides no information on a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2) or inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3). Task-related activations are not described (I4). Insufficient information to determine eligibility, so include for full-text review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed mental arithmetic, a problem-solving task (I2); includes age-matched healthy adult control group (I3); reports task-related brain activations (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study measuring brain activity while participants performed deductive reasoning (conditional and relational) and reports task-related activations. Abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants performing mathematical problem solving, includes healthy adult participants, and reports task-related brain activation (HIPS). Thus it satisfies I1–I4 and meets no exclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study with participants performing an analogy/semantic-fit judgment (a reasoning task), includes healthy young adult volunteers, and reports task-related brain activation (hippocampus, prefrontal, medial temporal). Fits inclusion criteria for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study and reports task-related brain activation during a virtual navigation task (meets I1 and I4). It is unclear from the abstract whether the virtual navigation task qualifies as a problem-solving or reasoning task per the review objective (I2 uncertain) and participant health status is not explicitly stated (I3 unclear). Because key inclusion (I2/I3) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, include for full-text review.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of healthy adult students performing mental calculation (a problem-solving task) and reports task-related brain activation (left angular gyrus). It therefore meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of geometric analogical processing (a reasoning/problem-solving task) in healthy participants and reports task-related BOLD activation and training-induced modulation. Therefore I1-I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Does not meet inclusion criterion I2: the task is navigation/object recognition in a virtual maze, not an explicit problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based PET), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 — participants did not perform a problem-solving or reasoning task (study investigates heat pain). Therefore excluded.

E2 met: sample consists of left-hemisphere stroke patients with aphasia and no healthy adult group. Inclusion met: I2 (human participants performed a non-verbal reasoning task, RCPM). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study; VLSM lesion mapping), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation from fMRI/PET).

Task-based PET study of a problem-solving task (modified Tower of London) including healthy adult controls and reporting task-related cerebral blood flow/activation changes over learning; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD contrasts during a problem-solving (insight into Chinese logogriphs) task, so I1, I2, and I4 are clearly met. The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI (BOLD responses) during a mental multidigit multiplication problem-solving task with reported cortical activation. It is unclear from the abstract whether participants were healthy adults, so full text is needed to confirm I3.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related hippocampal and striatal activation during navigation. Abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults nor clearly label the navigation as a problem-solving/reasoning task, so full-text review is needed to confirm I2 and I3.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing scientific problem-solving tasks and reports task-related brain activation. The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

PET study using a modified Tower of London problem-solving task in 12 healthy participants; reports task-related blood-flow activation changes and correlational analyses across learning. Meets I1 (PET), I2 (problem-solving task), I3 (healthy participants), and I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (human participants performed problem-solving task) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results via ERPs). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 not met — study used ERPs (EEG), not task-based fMRI or PET; I3 not demonstrated — abstract does not specify participants were healthy adults.

Excluded (E2): study involves adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing a reasoning/transitive inference task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult group reported).

This is a task-based PET study in human adults performing maze traversal (nonverbal planning/problem solving), reporting task-related brain activations. No exclusion criteria are met; abstract indicates a sample of eleven adults (presumed healthy). Recommend inclusion for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Exclusion IDs met: none (no exclusion criteria clearly met). Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task not evident — study investigates spatial encoding/pointing, not problem-solving), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated in abstract). Based on lack of evidence for I2, exclude.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task; task was inspiratory loading/respiratory stress).

Task-based whole-brain fMRI study of the Paced Auditory/Visual Serial Addition Task (problem-solving/serial addition), within-subject sample of healthy young adults (n=20), reporting task-related brain activation and deactivation maps. Meets I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

This is a task-based fMRI study of fluid intelligence components (induction, visualization, spatial relationships) — problem-solving/reasoning tasks — in healthy adult participants, and reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study (I1) using syllogistic reasoning (I2) and describes task-related brain activations (I4). The abstract does not explicitly state the participants were healthy adults (I3 not confirmed), so include for full-text review to confirm health status.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult males and females reporting task-related brain activation during virtual 3D maze navigation. Unclear whether maze navigation meets the review's definition of 'problem-solving or reasoning' (I2), so full-text review is needed to confirm.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving (Tower of London) task with reported task-related brain activation. It does not explicitly state participant health status, so include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult sample.

Task-based fMRI study using a virtual maze (I1) with healthy adult participants aged 40–55 (I3) and reports neural correlates measured with fMRI (I4). The abstract does not clearly state whether the virtual maze task meets the review’s ‘problem-solving/reasoning’ definition (I2 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Exclusion E2 met: participants are children (ages 8–10) with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (number-line/arithmetical tasks), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion I3 not met.

Task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning that reports task-related rostral PFC activations. Abstract does not state participant health/age, so include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

The study used task-based fMRI (I1) and reports task-related activations (I4). However, participants performed action observation/ToM tasks, not problem-solving or reasoning tasks (I2 not met). The abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are clearly met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants reported), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the abstract describes spatial coding/processing via verbal descriptions, not a problem-solving or reasoning task; there is no evidence participants performed problem-solving or reasoning. Excluded for not meeting I2.

EXCLUDED: Study used rats (non-human) — meets exclusion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based PET) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (human problem-solving/reasoning task) and I3 (includes healthy adult participants).

Study is a task-based PET investigation of maze learning (a problem-solving/visuospatial task) in 15 normal volunteers and reports regional cerebral blood flow activation differences between novel and practiced performance, meeting all inclusion criteria.
